R3812.summary: Kurz von Senftenau on the quartering of six imperial regiments and the Lower Saxon Kreistag: Banér's plundering will ruin the Stift Halberstadt, Duke Georg of Lüneburg will not resist; he sees no real Swedish or French wish for peace and great ill-feeling between Denmark and Sweden. Postscript on Arnim's visit after escaping Swedish captivity.
R3812.en:
Highborn Lord Count, gracious Lord.

My last of 27 January is at length; I must describe the illness, so that one may know how to direct the remedies
to it. [?The soldiery], since under the accommodation of the six regiments and the Circle diet [the matter] rests on the
following: the first is explained by Salis's letter sent to me, the second now rests on the outcome of the Circle
diet. As for Salis, I do not know whether the [?orders] have reached him, eventualiter, to take quarters in the
Halberstadt country, and that it may be settled against a future grant; the lack of means and the good inclination of
the land are not to be taken away before the Circle's resolution; so after the Circle's resolution it will go [...]
[?harder], for they will, e concluso, have the Circle resist then, as also nothing but a particular resistance. Banér
[...] the Circle [...]

R3811.summary: Nothing can be done with Duke Georg; France, Sweden and Holland plan an embassy to the King of Denmark to prevent a congress in Sweden; Duke August of Saxe-Lauenburg is said to seek Danish protection; Arnim denies plotting against the Peace of Prague and Kurz advises a protectorium. The letter carries an interlinear decipherment (summarised by Mírka in 2012).
R3811.en:
Most high-born Lord Count, gracious Lord,

In Duke Georg's affairs I cannot quite find my way. The enemy is across without resistance; against him [there are]
so many troops, though with rotten muskets, such as [...] did at that time, because one [hears] of neutralities here;
and here the failure to resist gives all the more suspicion. Whether it happens for lack of strength, and will be used
at its time and place hereabouts, remains to be seen. To defend the Elbe and the Weser is impossible for the Duke, and
they also take our subsidies for little friendship. I would wish Salis had better regiments with him, that could show
themselves to friend and foe. [...] whether among them some are not still reformed, which yet will not come up; the
part of the Lower Saxon Circle we must not let out of our possession, [and must] forbid the enemy to cross;

R3813.summary: Twenty-page memorandum: the enemy advances unopposed towards Salzwedel; a Kreistag broken up by the enemy is better than one concluded with express neutrality; Kurz advises a defensive strategy, distrusts Salvius, weighs a secret particular treaty with Sweden through Brandenburg or Denmark, and says France wants Lorraine, Alsace and even the imperial crown.
R3813.en:
High-born Lord Count, gracious lord.

I am still waiting for Herr Pfenz, who is hiding here; Wol[...] and my people are at Lüneburg; with the English king's [envoy] there is nothing [to be done]; the following of the Danes and Holsteiners was no bridge and no security. The enemy is coming over here quite unhindered and is moving up towards Salzwedel, so that the [?troops] under Salis and the artillery in the [?assigned] [?quarters] will not stay safe, or at least can [?withdraw]. Apart from Meirer's regiment nothing more has arrived here. Note: at the first crossing Winckel was in command, at the other Meirer.

On that, the offers we have made him have not moved him either, for the danger he may rightly fear under Swedish domination. If the [...] of Mainz should be [able] in its time to remedy [things] more surely than now, when fortune is with us.

R3814.summary: The Swedish agent Mithoff and the Danish mediation; safe-conducts; Lorraine, Mantua and Pomerania in pledge; Rákóczi said to take French money with the Turk's consent; Kurz defends his secret particular dealing with Mithoff and describes a secret post route via Ehrenberg and Wolfenbüttel.
R3814.en:
Most noble lord and gracious lord. After [...] three posts of Mithoff and the letter of Salvius at Leipzig had been
brought here without my [...], and opened, he handed them to me: the letters are mostly in cipher, at discretion.
Whether I have got fairly far with [?Mithoff], round about in laments, that one [...] to work off: they lay the blame
on me, they ask Salvius and hope for better from him; and he promised him [...] would do nothing until they came
again. It is added that Sweden will in this way let Denmark prescribe no laws to it, and force the safe-conducts as he wishes.
Sent over [the news] that Denmark had worked honestly in this. But that for the rest there is no hope, nor of naming
the day.

[...] they would have it by feudal right [...], whether not to bring it on the heirs of [?Gustavus] and the present
Queen alone; for the crown is immortal. 5.

R3815.summary: The King of Denmark is perplexed and perhaps stalling to avoid a conjunction with the Emperor; the Danish Reichsrat is irresolute; with 8-9,000 men the princes could deal with a starved, exhausted enemy; Salis sent to Hildesheim, Duke Georg, the Kreis resolution, Hatzfeldt.
R3815.en:
Most gracious Emperor and Lord. Your Imperial Majesty has no doubt lately most graciously received my letter sent off
[...]. Herewith comes the answer, and what has been further replied to it; I have not thought it Your Majesty's service
to answer everything it contains so [?exactly]. My few reports, and also what Sergeant-Major-General Count Puchheim and
Mandelslo put and brought before Banér, will explain more than enough [how] the whole imperial army [is] left to perish
while waiting for the Circle's [?resolution]. It could well have been done, for over the frozen Elbe the enemy's
crossing could hardly have been prevented without particular resistance. But whether an equal force would have been
[?needed], since the enemy [came] over here little by little by ship, that I doubt. But it is now a thing that has
happened;

R4625.summary: Memorandum on keeping the Lower Saxon Circle divided and holding Halberstadt, Magdeburg, Hildesheim and Wolfenbüttel; 8,000 Danish men in Holstein; three grades of Circle war; the imperial army is ruined.
R4625.en:
to raise. If one would rather bind oneself to the Circle than to the Emperor and the Empire, since this is and
always has been the only remedy, to keep the Circle disunited and thereby [...] the House of Saxony, so as to meet
[danger] to the whole Roman Empire: Halberstadt, Magdeburg, Hildesheim and Wolfenbüttel must keep us in the Circle and
keep the Empire its authority, if we ourselves do not want to abandon it. To do it ourselves, to exclude [others] from
it with little, what other estates do: it can be done, how easily two and three thousand men can be kept in these
places, if they are fed head for head, and the rest is received from them in [...] or Silesia. Politically, then, I am
not at all of the opinion that one should withdraw the troops, but rather add more [...], than six regiments;

R4645.summary: The Danish interposition and a possible conjunction with the Emperor: the King's distinctions proved mere lies; Count Pentz says the King must drop the mediation and denounce Sweden. With clear copies of two letters of Banér of 29 Jan 1639.
R4645.en:
[Salutation not read.]

Count Penz tells me [?it was] the beginning of the future conjunction that the King should give up the mediation and
[?denounce] this to the Crown of Sweden, and moreover that while the negotiations are delayed the one and the other
would happen, he [?also] would not do it. So the rupture of the negotiations is here the beginning of the
conjunction. I leave it undecided; our counsels stay with what I wrote lately. I have [?said] often [...]: if one does
not grasp by now that nothing can or will come of the negotiations, then I do not have the capacity to argue it
further; consequently [...] persuaded the King [...] good offices can be the hope of the congress, which [is the hope]
of peace; by the very admission of the confederation war has been declared on him; we are therefore now clearly
[?shut out] of the negotiations.

R4734.summary: The Danish mediation has expired and the King has his hands tied; the Lower Saxon Circle must contribute to war or to compensation; Stralsund or other lands might go to Brandenburg. Addressed to 'E. Excell.' (Schwarzenberg per DECODE).
R4734.en:
Image P2. … has [told] me … at … treaty … nothing … and will nothing … and therefore desired to confer with them what
⟨way to take, the interposition having expired⟩, towards dear peace.

Image P4, left. … could let nothing be heard about it, ⟨until every form of conjunction is assured. Let this be what⟩
may … and only in their means. Thus, however, one will not declare oneself … the same matter, and so causes that …
itself: ⟨the King remains the more [?unintrigued] in the matter⟩, and ⟨we now have a free hand to embrace as often as
[?]⟩, and one … therefore with complaint ⟨that one has been passed over [?] [?]⟩. I am sure that … nothing else shall
be ascribed by Your Excellency than … the 8th of April 1639.

Image P5. … in which I [have] nothing at all with Your Excellency …, that ⟨the interposition must [?] reach⟩; secondly,
what was reported … concerning the mediation:

R4736.summary: At the Danish court: the Danes complain that war in Austria is bought with peace in Lower Saxony while the Swedes stay in Mecklenburg and Pomerania; papers to be sent to Schwarzenberg; outward respect for the Emperor nowhere greater than at Glückstadt.
R4736.en:
Most high-born Lord Count,

They would not gladly let me go from here; ill satisfied and satisfied is against all their principles. What counsel
[...] of arms to [...] the maxim His Electoral Highness wants [...] to hold for ever: that the war in Austria is held
to be peace in Lower Saxony, [even] though the Swedes stay in Mecklenburg and Pomerania. With the best right we
could ask our most gracious lordship not to let Pomerania be ruined for us [...]. What will happen when we have done
everything? The return of our soldiers to Austria, or a new war in the armed [...] of the Empire, and those who then
join the [?Swedes]? For such bulwarks we give our sweat and blood, stake everything in compromise [...] we have. After
the Swedes have thoroughly exhausted us, [...] everything, [they] will not be content, nor do they even now hold the Swedes
[?back], or could drive them out of the Empire.

system: Homophonic cipher: 1-40 and letter/graphic signs for single letters (some for letter pairs), 41-100 for consonant+vowel syllables in a regular reverse-alphabet table, a few nulls.
